sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Amba Auto Sales and Services Limited; NSE SME; ISIN INE293601014. Research cutoff 2026-10-20. Dated quote ₹109.5 on 2026-10-19, not a live executable bid. Five-year nominal INR scenarios use a 15% analyst equity hurdle and ₹5 lakh illustrative position. Current scope and capital bridge are described in financial forensics and the linked model.

Gate conclusions: G 1 Integrity: Verify resolution of continuing GST reconciliation non-compliance and quantify associated exposure. G 2 Financial reliability: Audit unmodified; ongoing GSTR 9 C non-filing is a control/compliance concern, not evidenced material false accounts. Source and share/debt bridges reviewed; reserves and stress disclose uncertainty. G 3 Funding: Stress funding and obligations require completed historical reconstruction. G 4 Tradability: Dated NSE quote/lot and observed liquidity checked; spreads, circuits, restrictions and executable depth remain unverified.

Evidence confidence: historical_levels: high after source/scan checks; economic_growth: medium; governance: medium with unquantified GSTR 9 C exposure; current_capital_bridge: medium; investment_scenario: medium for conditional tax/deployment estimates; future realization uncertain; overall: medium for conditional scores; no observed material tax shortfall is assumed. Forecast uncertainty is distinct from accuracy of the underlying disclosures.

Official 2026-10-19 close ₹109.5; volume 1,000.0 shares, turnover ₹109,500, 1.0 trades, lot 1000, series ['SM']. This dated trade is not a live executable bid. 20-session mean/median daily turnover ₹1,884,905/₹1,539,700; conservative denominator is the lower. ₹5 lakh theoretical exit takes 16.24/6.49/3.25 sessions at 2%/5%/10% participation before whole-lot rounding. 60-session window has 59 observed and 1 absent sessions; no zero-filled liquidity conclusion until listing dates/missing records are reconciled. Not an exit guarantee: spreads, available bids, circuits, impact, settlement/surveillance and whole-lot minimum positions remain to be checked. [M1]

No ISIN match in the checked NSE ESM/ASM lists dated 20 October and GSM list dated 19 October. This is not blanket clearance from all restrictions or proof of executable liquidity. Other exchange measures, price bands, settlement series and live spreads still require review.

Official October 19 EOD indicators, effective next trading session October 21: Less than 100 unique PAN traded in previous 30 days; SME scrip is not regularly traded; High low price variation greater than 100 perc in previous 6 months. These cautions do not contradict the actual observed turnover history: generic irregular-trading status is not evidence of any particular missing session. PAN breadth and expired mandatory market-making can weaken executable depth even when daily turnover is present. [REG1][REGFMT]

Current implementation assessment L 4: Fully observed 20-session conservative turnover₹1,539,700 implies 6.49 days to exit₹5 lakh at 5%, startingL 5; one-point downgrade for₹109,500 lot and only one trade onOctober 19.60-session conditional median₹2,089,550 gives 4.79 days but one absent security row remains conditional. sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: FY 26 standalone revenue ₹268.6793 cr versus ₹242.3665 cr; PAT ₹14.0322 cr versus ₹7.7760 cr. Service income rose from ₹13.9799 cr to ₹22.6220 cr. The report attributes performance to services and more showrooms; that attribution is management explanation, not proof of repeatable same-store economics. Consolidation is not applicable. [S1]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The authorized Bajaj Auto and LG dealership relationships create access and local service infrastructure, but the brand and product economics belong to the OEMs. Bajaj territory is Bengaluru; agreements are non-exclusive and non-transferable, with expansion contingent on OEM allocation. Bajaj can terminate without cause on 30 days notice. The largest supplier represented 88.44% of FY 25 purchases and 91.36% in the nine months to December 2025. This is not customer diversification or bargaining power. Services can improve mix, but recurring service economics must be separated from financed vehicle and appliance inventory. [P1][S1]

The prospectus names Popular Vehicles and Services, Bikewo Green Tech and Resourceful Automobile. Popular is materially larger and consolidated, while the smaller peers are standalone; April 2 prices and FY 25 earnings are historical, not current valuation evidence. The prospectus also gives inconsistent peer P/E sets across adjacent tables: 27.12/11.59 in its industry range versus 30.68/6.90 in the detailed table. Accordingly no peer average is adopted. The meaningful operating comparison is OEM bargaining dependence, parts/service mix, inventory days, finance cost and store-level return on incremental working capital, not the highest traded multiple. Current Popular Vehicles annual evidence is reviewed below; negative peer earnings prevent meaningful P/E calibration. [P1]

Popular Vehicles FY 26 consolidated figures show about ₹6,381 cr revenue, ₹203 cr EBITDA, ₹12.5 cr net loss, ₹100 cr operating cash flow and ₹623 cr net debt. EBITDA margin was 3.2%, with interest and depreciation absorbing operating profit. It spans six OEMs and seven states, unlike Amba’s concentrated two/three-wheeler geography. It supports conservative dealership margin and funding scenarios, not a direct P/E comparison with a loss-maker. [PEER1]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: FY 23/FY 24/FY 25/FY 26 revenue is ₹112.9545/211.2282/242.3665/268.6793 cr; PAT ₹0.6383/2.8869/7.7760/14.0322 cr. Sales CAGR FY 23–26 is 33.5%, but latest growth slows to 10.86%; PAT growth is disproportionately margin-led. Reported CFO is −₹0.2392/−2.8334/−6.9259/+3.6771 cr. Four-year CFO/PAT = −6.3214/25.3334 = −0.250; the FY 23 operating gratuity opening adjustment is −₹0.1695 cr and does not alter the conclusion. FY 23–26 cash asset purchases ₹0.2301/2.5833/4.4386/1.6029 cr imply cumulative FCF proxy −₹15.1763 cr, before financing interest. Interest is classified in financing, so operating cash conversion overstates cash left for equity. FY 26 cash interest alone is ₹6.6984 cr. These are persistent weak cash realization and funding dependence, not evidence of misconduct. [P1][U1]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
FY 26 operating EBIT excluding other income₹25.9732 cr versus₹16.6164 cr. Standard 25% NOPAT₹19.4799 cr divided by average equity-plus-debt₹80.44375 cr gives 24.22%; incremental₹7.0176 cr/₹20.1535 cr is 34.82%. These are pre-IPO accounting proxies, not mature store cash returns. Four-year negative CFO and IPO expansion capital prevent extrapolating them. Annual EBITDA/ROCE presentations use inconsistent finance-cost bases, so calculations use the P&L finance cost₹7.4663 cr and exclude other income. Bonus 17:1 issued September 2025 requires a consistent share denominator. Promoter 13.05 m shares imply 71.22% of post-IPO 18.324 m, distinct from all pre-IPO holders’73.67%. [S1][P1]

The final prospectus provides 4,824,000 fresh shares at ₹135, gross proceeds ₹65.124 cr, expenses ₹6.2471 cr and net proceeds ₹58.8769 cr. Objects allocate ₹43 cr to working capital, ₹6.3173 cr to showrooms and renovation, and ₹9.5596 cr to general purposes. Working capital consumes 73.0% of net proceeds: this is primarily financing the dealership cycle, not a new manufacturing moat. Pre-issue shares 13.5 m become 18.324 m; original holders retain 73.67%. These are prospectus terms, not a subsequent utilization certificate. The prose incorrectly labels ₹6.2471 cr as net proceeds, but the table reconciles exactly, so this isolated drafting error is not an integrity failure. [P1]

The October 10 filing defers a proposed fund-raising board meeting for preparatory requirements; it does not approve or allot securities. No assumed new issue price or proceeds enters the denominator. July 10 agreements add three Bengaluru showrooms on ten-year leases. Combined monthly rent including the backup area is ₹2.55975 lakh, with 10% escalation after two years, and refundable deposits total ₹30 lakh. These are commitments, not evidence of sales already generated. [FUND][LEASE]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Auditor identifies continuing non-filing of required historical GSTR-9 C reconciliation statements. Related late fees/penalties/interest were unascertained, and absence of reconciliation increases risk around GST balances. Opinion is not modified, but this is not a clean bill of governance health. The auditor records NSE SME listing on 5 May 2026 as a subsequent event, so FY 26 balance-sheet capital is pre-IPO. [S1]

July 22 document, publishedJuly 28, explains IPOproceeds arrived afterMarch 31 and listingMay 5, so FY 26 IPO-use disclosure was inapplicable; it also rectifies PDF/XBRL typo. This reply is not itself an adverse governancefinding. Visually checked cash-flow page 4: FY 26/FY 25 CFO₹3.6771/−6.9259 cr; capex₹1.6029/4.4386 cr; FCFproxy₹2.0742/−11.3645 cr. FY 26 inventory absorbed₹8.0178 cr and payables repayment₹7.5466 cr. Two-year conversion−3.2488/21.8082=−0.149; dealership inventoryfunding and cashinterest₹6.6984 cr remain important. IPOcash afteryear-end must notbe added toFY 26 closingcash before capital/debt/proceedsbridge. [U1]

The prospectus discloses FY 24 auditor qualification because the auditor did not physically verify inventory, while management verification was reported under CARO. A restated unqualified presentation does not by itself prove the missing physical evidence was retrospectively obtained. It also discloses GSTR 9 delays for FY 23 and FY 24, with consultant explanations. GSTR 9 is not GSTR 9 C: FY 26 annual-report continuing GSTR 9 C non-filing and unascertained exposure remains a distinct unresolved item. Promoter-family borrowing and repayment flows are substantial, including FY 25 Vikash Kumar Lohia loans taken ₹30.1572 cr and repaid ₹30.1843 cr; gross flows are not closing exposure or revenue. Terms, interest, approvals and ultimate source need review before concluding arms-length treatment. No unsupported fraud allegation or automatic G 1 failure is made. [P1][S1]

September 18 corrigendum fixes committee meeting years and identifies Chetankumar Solanki, rather than independent director Raina Singh, as compliance officer. It states no financial-statement impact. These remediated drafting errors are not an independent integrity-failure basis. They do not resolve the separate GSTR 9 C or historical inventory-audit matters. [CORR][S1][P1]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
March debt₹61.7005 cr includes₹1.1825 cr current maturities already in short-term debt. The report ratio incorrectly uses all liabilities as debt; it is not our leverage numerator. Inventory₹57.3914 cr and receivables₹20.5610 cr dominate assets. Receivables summary labels them doubtful while aging calls all good under six months; this disclosure conflict needs clarification, not automatic write-off of all receivables. Cash₹3.4676 cr plus deposits₹2.5803 cr is dated March, not post-IPO free cash. [S1]

The GSTR 9 C matter is continuing non-filing with unascertained late fees, penalties and interest, plus a risk of undetected GST-balance misstatement. The audit opinion is unmodified and does not allege a particular substantive tax shortfall. Known GST demand is₹1.57 lakh (Note 31), not₹1.57 cr. Therefore non-filing alone does not justify an automatic critical hold or IAS NS. The base deducts₹5.0162 cr comprising the disclosed March income-tax provision₹4.8903 cr plus unprovided income-tax/GST/TDS demands₹0.1081/0.0157/0.0021 cr. No invented expected GSTR 9 C bill is included. Additional₹10/20/30 cr losses are explicitly hypothetical sensitivities, not estimates or statutory liability caps. Reassess promptly if a quantified assessment or adverse reconciliation emerges. [S1]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Using the prospectus post-issue 18.324 m shares, FY 26 PAT ₹14.0322 cr implies normalized-share EPS ₹7.6578, not the pre-IPO weighted EPS. At the dated ₹109.50 close, indicative equity value is ₹200.6478 cr and P/E 14.30 x. The 18.324 m denominator also matches the official October 19 NSE security master; IPO net cash is not added again to equity value or assumed still free. A five-year 15% return requires terminal value ₹220.25 per share without dividends. At an assumed 12 x exit P/E, that requires EPS ₹18.35, or 19.1% annual EPS growth; at 15 x, EPS ₹14.68, or 13.9%. These are reverse hurdles, not forecasts. A 3% PAT margin on unchanged FY 26 sales gives PAT ₹8.0604 cr, EPS ₹4.399 and 10 x value ₹43.99, about 60% below the dated quote. This severe-downside sensitivity excludes additional funding dilution and is not a full linked model. The linked scenario and debt bridge complement these reverse hurdles; conditional IAS incorporates conservative tax/deployment reserves and sensitivities. [P1][U1][M1]

Base/bear/bull conditional five-year IRRs are 12.00%/-25.67%/31.60%; terminal prices₹193.00/₹24.85/₹432.23. The annual model explicitly bridges IPO financing, working capital, interest, capex and debt. Conditional IAS is now scored with disclosed tax/deployment sensitivities. Non-filing creates uncertainty, but the unmodified opinion and small identified demand do not establish an unbounded material tax shortfall. Capital raise deferred October 10 adds contingent dilution risk, but no unapproved shares are assumed. [S1][P1][FUND]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
Analyst stress: dealer competition or manufacturer incentives compress gross margin while showroom leases/payroll and vehicle inventory funding persist. Monitor service gross profit separately from pass-through vehicle sales, same-store volumes, ageing inventory, OEM concentration, floorplan borrowing and whether GST filings/liabilities are actually resolved. Do not call a bonus issue economic dilution; reconstruct split/bonus-adjusted EPS and post-IPO shares.

Bear terminal₹24.85 and severe zero indicate severe potential capital impairment from margin compression, working-capital stretch and funding loss. IPO capital is substantial protection, but cannot make the entry resilient to combined stresses.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: At₹109.50, five-times/ten-times prices are₹547.50/₹1,095. At 15 x terminal earnings and 1.8324 cr shares, required PAT is₹66.88/₹133.77 cr, versus₹14.03 cr FY 26: roughly 36.7%/57.0% annual growth. With 5% PAT margin, sales₹1,338/₹2,675 cr would be required. Store capacity, OEM permission, working-capital funding and dilution make this an unsupported upside claim, not a forecast. [S1][P1][M1]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Track new/service units separately, service gross margin, inventory aging and funding cost; obtain GSTR 9 C filing and quantified exposure; reconcile₹43 cr working-capital proceeds and showroom spending with subsequent balance sheet; review proposed fundraising terms before denominator updates; distinguish corrected committee dates from actual reporting-control improvement. Reference₹5 lakh liquidation at 5% participation takes 6.49 days using the fully observed 20-session median₹15.397 lakh; lot₹1.095 lakh and only one trade onOctober 19 require conservative execution assumptions. The 60-session sample has one security-level absence, not a missing whole-market file. No blanket surveillance or spread clearance is claimed. [S1][P1][FUND][M1]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Bajaj-led Bengaluru dealership with verified unit/service growth and improving operating profits, but persistent historical cash absorption, substantial inventory funding and unresolved GSTR 9 C exposure. IPO capital materially changes the balance-sheet capacity; conditional scenarios account for it, without pretending its current deployment or tax downside is verified. BQS 4.84, GQS 5.0 capped at 5 by persistent CASH 3, conditional IAS 4.01. Historical compliance warning remains; it is not treated as proof of a material unlimited tax demand. Reference₹5 lakh liquidity and explicit cash/debt assumptions apply.

Final published measures: BQS 4.84; GQS 5.0; IAS 4.01. Any change in price, funded cash deployment, share count or execution restrictions requires recomputation; these are conditional research classifications, not a trade instruction.

valuation.status: Conditional scenarios using an IPO-adjusted March bridge, not an observed October balance sheet
assumption_basis: Net IPO proceeds are a dated financing bridge, not claimed October cash. General corporate purpose allocation ₹9.5596cr is excluded as potentially spent. ₹5.0162cr is settlement of disclosed March income-tax provision₹4.8903cr plus separately unprovided income-tax/GST/TDS demands₹0.1081/0.0157/0.0021cr. The provision is already net of TDS; contingent demands are expressly unprovided. It is not an estimate of GSTR9C penalties; stress adds hypothetical₹10/30cr losses. Revenue-authority assets₹0.7107cr are excluded from operating WC because their tax type/offset availability is unspecified; zero recovery is the conservative base, full recovery is a separate sensitivity. Preliminary expenses₹1.2195cr are also excluded from operating WC as noncash deferred costs.

₹43cr IPO working-capital allocation is not treated as distributable surplus: cash first supports inventory/receivables and scheduled showroom investment; remaining cash is modeled to repay working-capital debt. If actual deployment differs, scenarios must be recomputed. No double count of net proceeds in terminal equity.
Opening debt includes current maturities already within short-term borrowings. Deposit investment ₹2.5803cr and noncash investments excluded from surplus. Operating reserve remains excluded.

Base EBIT8% is below FY26 operating9.67%, growth12% near current sales trajectory, WC30% near broad FY26 balance-sheet ratio. Bear4.5% and severe2% margins acknowledge dealership operational leverage and peer losses. Bull10% assumes durable service mix and execution, not sector norm.

Tax25% on positive PBT, interest10.5% on opening debt, depreciation0.75% and capex1.2% of sales with first-year minimum₹6.3173cr; no dividend, new equity or approval of deferred fundraising assumed. New borrowing is funding required, not facilities assured.
